rationale: The gating logic is coherent and correctly signed, but it is close to a rediscovery of the well-documented asset-growth anomaly conditioned on profitability (the FF5/q-factor investment-profitability interaction), and the indicator sets roughly half the cross-section to exactly zero, so quintile breakpoints will collapse onto a degenerate zero mass and make portfolio composition unstable.

This is simply free cash flow to assets, a long-published measure (cash-based operating profitability / FCF anomaly) with no genuine cross-theme structure beyond one subtraction, so it is both a rediscovery and too trivial to be worth a test slot.

The denominator (capx + aqc) approaches zero for asset-light and non-investing firms, so the ratio explodes and its sign flips arbitrarily with negative OCF, making the cross-sectional ordering non-monotonic in the hypothesized economics and only cosmetically repaired by 1% winsorization.

A genuinely cross-theme construction whose expression matches the stated hypothesis and sign, with sensible rank-then-difference scaling; the main risks are noisy five-year trends in capx/ppent and coverage loss from the long estimation window.

Despite the "joint profile" claim, nested SUMRANK is a purely additive (and unequally weighted) blend of three separately documented effects — profitability, cash holdings, and capacity-growth — so it tests a generic quality composite rather than any conditional cross-theme mechanism.

Because both factors are bounded ranks, the product's low end is dominated by unprofitable firms rather than by non-expanding profitable firms, so the long leg loads on the wrong side of the profitability anomaly and works directly against the expected negative sign.
